title: 2-Year Treasury Note auction (November new issue) — the front-end sale that opens Thanksgiving week's three-day coupon block
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) and its text layer decompressed stream-by-stream — NOT carried from the proposing sweep's transcription. Row reads verbatim `2-Year NOTE Thursday, November 19, 2026 Monday, November 23, 2026 Monday, November 30, 2026` (announcement / auction / settlement) with NO trailing `R`, so a new issue. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing coupon-auction convention and is NOT separately sourced. The same 11-19 announcement carries three more coupon rows read in the same fetch — `2-Year FRN R` and `5-Year NOTE` on Tuesday 11-24, `7-Year NOTE` on Wednesday 11-25 — and the schedule's own holiday line reads `Holiday - Thursday, November 26, 2026 - Thanksgiving Day`. STAYS ESTIMATE on the one limit that actually applies at D-75: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this sale is 71 days from its own announcement. The confirming primary is the 2026-11-19 announcement itself. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-09), which read the single prior proposal (`proposals/treasury-2y-note-2026-11-23.from-treasury-20y-bond-2026-11-18.json`, 2026-09-08) first, per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THAT PROPOSAL, both primary-read. (1) IMPACT RAISED low -> medium, matching the two sibling 2Y sales this calendar already tracks (treasury-2y-note-2026-09-22, treasury-2y-note-2026-10-26); the proposal's own note argues the case for it ('the 2-Year is the tenor that actually prices policy') and then files `low`. Practical effect is the 21-day cadence band instead of 30. (2) THE SIZE CAUTION IS RESOLVED THE OTHER WAY: the proposal carried $69B second-hand off `sb0590`'s grid. Read direct today (home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0590, HTTP 200), that grid runs `May-26 Jun-26 Jul-26 Aug-26 Sep-26 Oct-26` and STOPS — there is no November row anywhere in the release, so no Treasury document published today names this auction's size. $69B is an EXPECTATION from 29 consecutive $69B 2Y prints (2024-04-23 -> 2026-08-25, fiscaldata, zero deviations) plus the release's verbatim flat guidance ('Treasury anticipates maintaining nominal coupon and FRN auction sizes for at least the next several quarters'); the published figure arrives at the 2026-11-04 refunding, and nothing in this entry licenses a size claim before then. THE FINDING THAT EARNS THIS EVENT ITS LEDGER — the sibling 10-26 ledger's -6.07bp far-from-FOMC auction-day prior is a REGIME property, not a structural one, and 2026-11-23 is the first clean test of it. Extending that study out of sample (all 320 nominal 2Y auctions since 2000 against 6,674 par-curve sessions, both pulled today): 2023+ auction days close -4.70bp (t = -4.60, n=44) but 2000-2022 auction days close +0.38bp (t = +1.34, n=276) — wrong sign, insignificant, and the difference between the two windows is itself decisive (permutation p < 0.00001, 100k draws; diff-in-diff vs same-window non-auction sessions -4.94bp now against +0.43bp then). The rolling 24-auction window dates the switch to 2022-2023 and shows it stable since (t between -2.8 and -6.0 for every window ending 2024+) — but the same series has produced two earlier significant episodes (2000-2001 at -2.79, t = -2.96; 2002-2004 at +3.00, t = +2.28) and BOTH decayed. SECOND FINDING, A CLEAN NEGATIVE: the Thanksgiving-week discount does not exist. Far-from-FOMC 2Y auctions inside Thanksgiving week look worse than others on the full 2000+ sample (+2.11bp vs -0.68bp, permutation p = 0.043, n=18) and that entire gap is pre-2010 — 2002 (+16bp), 2003 (+8bp) and 2008 (+22bp). Every modern cut kills it: 2010+ p = 0.84, 2013+ p = 0.95, 2018+ p = 0.94. Demand does not deteriorate either (bid-to-cover 2.63 in-week vs 2.62 out, 2018+), and the two $69B-era Thanksgiving-week sales covered 2.77 and 2.68 against an era median of 2.64. Do NOT discount this auction for the holiday week. THIRD — THIS IS THE CLEANEST ATTRIBUTION DAY IN THE NOVEMBER BLOCK: 2026-11-23 carries ZERO other tracked events, where 11-18 carries six including the 2:00pm FOMC minutes that its own 20Y ledger says contaminate that print, and 11-25 carries five (PCE, GDP-Q3-second, durable goods, new home sales, beige book) because Thanksgiving pulls the Thursday/Friday releases forward onto the Wednesday. The only same-day competition is the 13-week and 26-week bill auctions, which price at 11:30am ET. Far from FOMC: the next meeting is fomc-2026-12-09, D+16, so the pre-FOMC pin the 10-26 sibling measured does not apply here. Read-it-do-not-trade-it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed. Ledger: docs/research/events/treasury-2y-note-2026-11-23.md.
